detail:
O is held by the quantum: bp-app.lisp:242 fnn-quantum-bp -> fnn-bpapp-accept-locked (bp-app.lisp:137/143) -> fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission (owner.lisp:5337) -> fnn-owner-commit-queued-locked (owner.lisp:4730; its docstring: 'the caller already holds'). At owner.lisp:~4747 it calls fnn-owner-batch-job inline; fnn-owner-batch-job (owner.lisp:4633) says 'off the owner mutex (the syncer thread's body, or inline in a bound submission's quantum)'. The code comment at the call site itself says 'this path's I/O under the owner is HOST-LIFECYCLE's to retire'. Chains: fnn-owner-batch-effect (owner.lisp:4590) :append -> fnn-log-sealed-append (io.lisp:9255) -> fnn-log-append (io.lisp:7733) -> fnn-log-pwrite (io.lisp:7266: lseek, then write(2) via fnn-write-range); :extend -> fnn-log-sealed-extend -> fnn-log-preallocate (io.lisp:7290 posix_fallocate, :7298 lseek); :fence -> fnn-owner-batch-fence -> fnn-log-fdatasync (io.lisp:7275). Also owner.lisp:4740 fnn-owner-commit-start-locked (owner.lisp:4474) -> fnn-log-seal-capture (io.lisp:9214) -> fnn-log-await-sync (io.lisp:9195): sb-thread:condition-wait on the log lock's CV releases only the log lock, not O; it blocks only if a previous batch is still :syncing, which the gate's in-flight admission (owner.lisp:4720-ish docstring) is meant to exclude, so this key is held-but-normally-instant.
Keys: R2|fnn-log-pwrite|O:sb-posix:lseek, R2|fnn-log-fdatasync|O:sb-alien:alien-funcall, R2|fnn-log-preallocate|O:sb-alien:alien-funcall, R2|fnn-log-preallocate|O:sb-posix:lseek, R2|fnn-log-await-sync|O:sb-thread:condition-wait. (fnn-durable-barrier O keys under LOCK-R2-LIVE-RECONFIGURE-IO may also include the :fence path's fnn-log-fence -> fnn-log-make-durable -> fsync-file/dir; not separately traced.)
Hazard: every bound submission or BP transit that finds queued members commits inline: the owner mutex is held across a log write, fallocate and fdatasync. This is the exact disk stall the pipelined commit (lane log-2, syncer thread) was built to take off O.
fix: Deleted fnn-owner-commit-queued-locked and its step classifier, and deleted fnn-log-take :full inline fallback. Bound control, hybrid and BP submissions use the same derived START/off-owner job/COMPLETE driver as the committer; the held continuation runs only after its barrier. The new append worker also runs outside O. No scoped R2 exception or baseline edit.
notes: Not fixed in lane/lock-owner-class; design question, state stays open. fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission (owner.lisp) and fnn-owner-complete-bp-transit-submission call fnn-owner-commit-queued-locked, which must finish START/barrier/COMPLETE before the caller's own submit-callback runs, and both are reached from callers that hold O up the stack (bp-app.lisp:143 via fnn-bpapp-accept-locked inside fnn-quantum-bp; hybrid-control.lisp:166; owner.lisp:5604). Retiring the inline barrier means returning from the held quantum between START and the submission, which the callers' straight-line sequence (submit, take, intent, flush, Store attempt, resolution) does not allow, and the commit step table (fnn-owner-commit-step-action :idle) is written for an idle owner with no gate phase. Needs: ACL2 statement of the bound-submission as a two-quantum sequence (commit-then-submit) with the gate phase in between, or a recorded decision that a bound submission commits inline with the stated bound.

Key the checker was blind to until it resolved the *fnn-write-syscall* seam (LOCK-CHECKER-HOST-WRAPPER-IO-BLIND): R2|fnn-write-range|O:sb-unix:unix-write, the log frame write itself (fnn-log-pwrite io.lisp:7350 -> fnn-write-range), reached from the same inline commit chain and from fnn-bpapp-deliver (bp-app.lisp:248). Retiring the inline path removes it.

n-gc-pipeline code-phase scoped closure: the inline queued path and its action helper have no host definitions or calls. Current lock report compared with read-only train31 4976a4b53 control adds ZERO finding keys. The global checker remains red (69 new finding rows,4 stale,4 pre-existing BP callback audit moves); fdatasync/pwrite under-O keys also belong to independent direct bound Store commits and therefore do not disappear globally when this queue route is deleted. Those paths are not certified fixed by this item. Full-world host load and native POST latency gate are recorded separately in planning/design/gc-pipeline/RESULTS.md; N owns the latter.
scenario: A BP application delivery (or any bound submission with queued members) takes the inline path: O held across pwrite+fdatasync; a slow device stalls readers and control for the fdatasync duration.
